entry.title: The agent that searched once: agentic RAG, counted
entry.summary: Give a small model a search tool and permission to use it as often as it likes, and it searches once, in 30 runs out of 30. It beats one-shot RAG by one answer in thirty, at 2.7 times the tokens, and both score zero on the questions that need a second search.

entry.title: The 503 test: what a model outage does to an agent loop
entry.summary: Fail one model call in ten and a naive agent loop crashes 14 runs of 36. Add retries and the crashes vanish, six runs never stop, and the tokens go up ten times. Without classification and budgets, retries turn an outage into a bill.

entry.title: Seven attacks, four defences: what each one buys
entry.summary: One agent, one poisoned supplier document, seven ways of asking for the secret. A word filter stops two attacks and breaks two jobs. A rule on the e-mail tool stops six. Changing one operator stops the seventh, and proves less than it seems.

entry.title: Payload splitting: when the detector and the model read different pages
entry.summary: An attacker cuts an injection in the middle of a token and puts one unrelated line between the halves. Every pattern goes blind; the model reads straight through. The fix comes from network intrusion detection.
